title: Quarterly operational runway: commitment calendar for Hosted API + model lineup
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a concrete quarterly commitment calendar and operational runway that links Hosted API lineup decisions to capacity hedging, canary windows, and rollback policies. This ticket formalizes a repeatable cadence for (1) committing model rotations, (2) scheduling canaries and staged rollouts, (3) defining contingency lanes when capacity or regressions occur, and (4) aligning SLA/SLO cost buckets with model tiers.
objectives: Define a daily/weekly/monthly cadence (commitment calendar) for model lineup decisions that product, infra, and research can commit to
Surface clear guardrails for canary windows, rollback triggers (quality regressions or latency spikes), and capacity hedges tied to forecasted demand
Produce a cross-functional runbook that maps Hosted API route tiers to model variants and pre-approved fallback variants
Deliver a lightweight dashboard view for stakeholders to see upcoming commitments, canary schedules, and contingency lanes
scope: Hosted API model catalog only (dedicated/private covered in follow-up)
Model rotation scheduling and commit windows for Q2 2026
Operational runbook (canary > ramp > GA > rotation), rollback criteria, and handoff checklist
Stakeholder sync process and escalation path for cross-team decisioning
success_metrics: Reduce unexpected emergency rollbacks due to model regressions by 50% within the quarter
Commitment calendar coverage: 90% of lineup rotations have an assigned canary window and fallback variant
Time-to-decision for model rotation requests reduced to <= 48 hours for Tiers 1-2
Dashboard adoption: weekly viewers >= 10 (PMs, Eng leads, SRE, Research)
milestones: 2026-03-05: Draft commitment calendar template and decision matrix (internal review)
2026-03-18: Cross-functional review with Eng/SRE/Research — finalize rollback triggers
2026-03-28: Implement minimal dashboard prototype and calendar export in Console
2026-04-07: Runbook published to Confluence and dry-run on model rotation for staging fleet
2026-04-15: Q2 lineup committed and calendar published to stakeholders
risks: Forecast inaccuracy: committing lineup without accurate traffic forecasts could cause under-provisioning
Incomplete fallback variants for some models (missing quantized/low-cost variants) could extend rollback time
Cross-team bandwidth: Eng/SRE may be overloaded during calendar windows leading to missed canaries
mitigation: Embed capacity hedges (burst pools) as part of commit windows; require gate for rotations that exceed X qps
Inventory fallback variants during pre-commit checklist and require beta validation for any new variant
Reserve a weekly "commit window" meeting slot; assign clear owners for canary playbook steps
rollout_plan: Publish commitment calendar draft and invite feedback (PM / Research / SRE) — iteration 1
Lock canary guardrails (latency/quality thresholds, alert rules) and add to runbook
Instrument Console dashboard: upcoming commitments, last-reported SLOs, fallback readiness flag
Dry-run a staged model rotation on non-prod fleet and capture timings & playbook gaps
Flip commit calendar to 'published' state and schedule the first Q2 rotation per calendar
stakeholders: Customer success (for enterprise customers with pinned models)
notes: This ticket focuses on repeatability and operational clarity rather than deeply changing model selection logic.
Follow-up tickets should add Dedicated and Private release lane alignment and legal/compliance sign-off for regulated customers.
Consider adding a lightweight SLO budget visualization per model variant to the dashboard in a later iteration.
